subject.title: feat(chat): rewind and fork a session from a message bubble

question: Should OpenClaw expose `sessions.rewind` and `sessions.fork` as permanent gateway RPCs for transcript-only session rewinds, with external tool effects intentionally left unchanged?
rationale: The implementation creates a new user-facing recovery mode and public protocol contract; tests can validate mechanics but cannot decide the long-term product/API commitment or UX wording for irreversible external side effects.

options.title: Sponsor the public session API
options.body: Keep the two additive RPCs, require live UI proof, and merge the documented transcript-only rewind behavior.

options.title: Keep it Control-UI internal
options.body: Redesign the feature behind an existing internal/session capability rather than expanding the supported gateway method surface.

options.title: Pause for a narrower recovery design
options.body: Defer the feature until maintainers define the desired rollback semantics and user-facing safety model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the public session API
recommendation.body: Keep the two additive RPCs, require live UI proof, and merge the documented transcript-only rewind behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied feature history shows this contributor owns the proposed implementation and can provide the technical context for the API decision.
